role: Canada's food system is undergoing rapid digitalization (precision ag, cloud-connected machinery, automated processing, online retail) while CSA Group's research programme with the Community Safety Knowledge Alliance (CSKA) found the food value chain **largely not implementing cybersecurity standards** — a critical-infrastructure sector with consumer-scale cyber maturity.

name: CyberTracker
geography: global (Cape Town, South Africa origin; used by Indigenous communities and community-science projects worldwide)
role: Expert trackers (the Kalahari San origins are the founding case) hold knowledge that paper forms and scientific protocols can't capture without stripping its structure.

name: DESIS 2.0 — Digitally Enabled Seed Information System (Nepal)
geography: Nepal; national seed-sector infrastructure across federal, provincial, and local institutions
role: National digital seed information system; began as CIMMYT/USAID-supported, now under Nepal's Seed Quality Control Center

name: DFO aquaculture and sea-lice open reporting (BC datasets)
role: Open-net pen salmon farming is Canada's most contested food-production controversy, and its environmental performance (sea lice, fish health, transfers, antimicrobial use, mortality) is the evidence base of that debate.

name: Alibaba ET Agricultural Brain
role: Alibaba Cloud's ET Agricultural Brain (launched at The Computing Conference 2018, Shanghai) applies company-developed AI — visual recognition, voice recognition, real-time environmental monitoring — to agriculture, initially pig farming and fruit/vegetable production.

name: Western University FAST Lab open scientific instrumentation (OSSEI)
geography: London, Ontario, Canada (Western University FAST Research Group); designs published globally, some with independent use
role: Scientific instruments — analytical balances, turbidity meters, magnetic stirrer hotplates, gas/environmental monitors — are priced for funded laboratories, not for under-resourced research, teaching, field water-quality work, or small operations.

name: fiboa and EuroCrops
geography: international (fiboa datasets span 30+ countries; EuroCrops 16 EU countries) — **Canada absent from both**
role: Agricultural field boundaries — the geometry beneath every farm program, subsidy, and remote-sensing analysis — are state-held administrative data that neither North American government publishes.

name: Framework Agreement on First Nation Land Management (land-code regime)
role: Indian Act land administration — 44 land-related sections administered by the federal Crown — leaves First Nations governing their own reserve lands under someone else's law.

name: Global Open Data for Agriculture and Nutrition (GODAN)
geography: global; Africa-relevant agricultural and nutrition data coordination
role: GODAN addresses fragmented agricultural and nutrition data, weak coordination, and the need to make relevant data more accessible and usable.

name: Holos — Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada
geography: Canada; federal public research and extension infrastructure
role: Holos is a whole-farm greenhouse-gas emissions model and decision-support software project associated with Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada.

name: ICAR Animal Data Exchange (ADE) standard
geography: international (10+ countries implementing; Canadian governance participation)
role: Animal Data Exchange (ADE) JSON standard for livestock/milk-recording data (Apache-2.0, ADE Working Group)

name: ISOBlue 2.0
geography: United States (Purdue University origin; AFIN — Agricultural Informatics Lab; open hardware + software, replicated internationally)
role: Open design pattern (data and control on the farmer's device by design) proven in tractors and transplanted to greenhouses

name: JBS ransomware attack (2021)
geography: multinational — US, **Canada (Brooks, AB)**, Australia; world's largest meat processor (~one-fifth of global meat supply)
role: **None.** Kill-floor scheduling, carcass tracking, payroll, and logistics are proprietary and centralized at corporate servers — the attack vector was exactly that centralization.

name: Maple Leaf Foods ransomware attack (2022)
geography: Canada (Mississauga, ON HQ; ~14,000 employees; Canada, US, Asia)
role: **None.** ERP, plant scheduling, payroll, and supply-chain systems are proprietary and centralized.

name: Monitorfish (France)
geography: France (national production system); open source internationally
role: Fisheries monitoring and control: the state's Fisheries Monitoring Center must fuse VMS positions, declarative fishing activity (ERS/FLUX), regulated-area rules, fleet-segment risk, prior notifications, and inspection records into a real-time operational picture for enforcement.

name: NAPDC / Ag Data Coalition (Growers Agricultural Data Cooperative)
role: US farmers' data is stored, shared, and monetised through vendor platforms that often claim perpetual rights.

name: OpenEMS (Open Source Energy Management System)
geography: Germany-origin (OpenEMS Association e.V., Deggendorf); deployed internationally across commercial, industrial, agricultural, and residential microgrids
role: Farm microgrids and rural energy installations increasingly combine solar PV inverters, battery energy storage systems (BESS), combined heat and power (CHP) biogas gensets, heat pumps, cold-storage compressors, and EV/machinery chargers.

name: OpenEPCIS (epcis-repository-ce)
geography: international (maintainer in Germany; food & beverage a target industry)
role: Event-based supply-chain traceability at processing scale: FSMA 204 KDE/CTE records, meat and cattle traceability frameworks, and the coming EU digital product passport all need an EPCIS event repository.

name: OpenFlexure Microscope (Agrifood Soil & Pathology)
geography: International (UK, Tanzania, Panama, Latin America / Gathering for Open Science Hardware - GOSH & REGOSH network)
role: Assessing biological soil health (nematodes, mycorrhizae, fungal-to-bacterial ratios) and screening for plant pathogens (spores, foliar blights, waterborne contaminants) requires laboratory-grade microscopy with precision sample positioning.

name: openreactor & open-source-bioreactor — FAST open bioprocess instrumentation
geography: London, Ontario, Canada (Western University FAST Research Group); software published openly, hardware design source on GitHub
role: Small-scale fermentation, bioprocessing and thermal work (melting, curing) needs reproducible control of temperature, mixing, dosing and water chemistry, plus a record of each run.

name: OpenSourceSeeds / Open Source Seed Licence (OSSL)
role: Contractual open seed licence extending obligations to derivatives and compatible with seed law; the enforceable counterpart to OSSI's pledge, with no enforcement case located

name: Open Source Range (OSR) GPS Collar
geography: United States / Global (rangeland ecology and extensive livestock pasture research)
role: Tracking cattle, sheep, and goat movement across expansive rangelands is crucial for rangeland conservation, predator monitoring, and grazing optimization.

name: Open Agroecology Lab (REGOSH)
geography: Argentina (Mendoza, Buenos Aires, Córdoba and other provinces); networked with GOSH and OpenTEAM internationally
role: Open-source digital infrastructure for agroecology (farmOS + SurveyStack + open sensing) with co-designed data governance; Shuttleworth-funded; activity documented 2018-2023, post-2023 unverified

name: ROMI — Robotics for Microfarms
geography: Europe; field sites near Paris and Barcelona
role: ROMI develops robotic tools to assist organic, diversified, human-scale vegetable farms with physically demanding or repetitive work such as weeding, crop monitoring, and plant phenotyping.

name: SAMA (Solar Alone Multi-objective Advisor) — FAST open microgrid sizing tool
geography: London, Ontario, Canada (Western University FAST Research Group); developed for global use
role: Designing a farm- or community-scale hybrid renewable microgrid (PV, battery, generator, grid-tie) requires techno-economic sizing — choosing component capacities that minimise lifetime cost under a site's load profile, weather, degradation and utility billing structure.

name: SAOS (Scottish Agricultural Organisation Society)
geography: Scotland / UK; cooperative federation of ~56 primary agricultural co-ops (est. 1905; ~600 primary co-op directors; group turnover >£4.5M, 31 staff, McMahon 2022)
role: Farm data is siloed, locked into vendor platforms, and its value accrues outside farming.

name: Sinong (神农, Shennong) — Agricultural Foundation Model
geography: China (Nanjing Agricultural University); open weights distributed globally via ModelScope and GitHub
role: Sinong is described as China's first open-source, agriculture-specific large language model: a vertical "agricultural brain" trained on agricultural knowledge to support farmers, agronomists, breeders, veterinarians, and agricultural economists with domain-accurate reasoning rather than generic chatbot responses.

name: SMART (Spatial Monitoring and Reporting Tool)
geography: global (60+ countries; built and maintained by a partnership of WWF, WCS, ZSL, Frankfurt Zoological Society, North Carolina Zoo, Panthera, Re:wild and others)
role: Community monitors and enforcement patrols need standardized, analyzable records of what is seen, harvested, and threatened in the field — collected offline, synced intermittently, and usable by non-specialists.

name: WAGRI (Agricultural Data Collaboration Platform)
role: Japan's WAGRI is a state-built agricultural data platform that links data and services through APIs so that farmers, machinery makers, ICT vendors, and service companies can collaborate on data-driven agriculture.

name: Grain Bikes (bicycle-powered grain processing machines)
geography: US Northeast (Massachusetts); plans freely buildable anywhere
role: Small farms and micro-mills need threshing, winnowing, dehulling, and coarse milling without grid power or four-figure equipment.

name: IBI open-source biochar technologies (aggregator)
geography: Global aggregator; hosted by International Biochar Initiative; individual designs span US, Australia, and other regions

name: Western University FAST Lab / WIRED open-source agrivoltaics hardware
geography: London, Ontario, Canada (Western University); design commons published globally via Appropedia and Open Science Framework (OSF)
role: Commercial solar photovoltaic (PV) racking is engineered for utility-scale steel ground mounts rather than active farm operations, and proprietary agrivoltaic tracking/mounting systems carry high capital premiums that raise levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) for farmers.
